sources.title: Human History Map: Cappadocia index and decoded imported outlines
sources.note: Own-project factual-data exception. Exact index -323 to -200, two identical feature bounds. Tests: Gazioura, Amaseia, Ankara and Bursa inside; Mazaca, Tyana, Kınık Höyük, Göreme and sampled Sinope point outside. Does not establish historical territorial ownership.

sources.title: Silvia Panichi: Cappadocia through Strabo’s eyes (2005)
sources.note: Publisher chapter summary directly read and indexed. Distinction of wider geographical Cappadocia from two successor kingdoms; horse breeding, Iranian aristocratic background, circa 250 BCE royal title. Not a claim of full chapter access. DOI 10.1017/CBO 9780511616099.014 grouped with this URL.

sources.title: Oxford Classical Dictionary: Ariarathes
sources.note: Original publisher indexed entry checked; direct fetch failed. Early family under Persian and Macedonian sway; Ariarathes I died circa 322, II circa 280; independence in mid-third century under Ariaramnes or co-ruling Ariarathes III. No precise restoration date asserted.

sources.title: A. Shapur Shahbazi: Ariyāramna, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct full entry, numbered section 5 on Cappadocian dynast. Royal intermarriages, headgear/horseman coins, exact Roman Ariaramnou and explicit gloss belonging to Ariaramnes. Article’s numbering of Ariarathes and exact 256 date are not adopted; chronology checked with OCD.

sources.title: British Museum: Ariaramnes copper-alloy coin, 1915,0407.15
sources.note: Original museum indexed catalogue read; direct fetch cache miss. Circa 280 to 230 BCE, Tyana, 19 mm, 4.68 g, leather-helmet head and spear-bearing horseman. Inscriptions field not extracted; this object is not claimed as the independently transcribed Berlin specimen.

sources.title: Warwick Wroth: Catalogue of Greek Coins of Galatia, Cappadocia and Syria (British Museum, 1899)
sources.note: Original downloaded scan; printed page xxv/PDF page 23 visually checked as bmc 23.png. Berlin bronze entry, Ariaramnes head and rider with spear, printed Greek legend. Modern Unicode transcription of type lettering. Use only the attested legend/object; old exact chronology and nearby disputed Ariarathes III silver attribution excluded.

sources.title: Kınık Höyük excavation team: Excavations at Kınık Höyük, 39. Kazı Sonuçları Toplantısı 2 (2017)
sources.note: Author-uploaded original full report read. Printed pages 592 to 593: Operation B, early/middle Hellenistic B 4 houses; earlier B 5 food room Br 9 and workshop Br 10. Level B 3 defensive wall is later and excluded. Page 595 Operation D ovens not assigned an exact date. No evidence of a household kinship census or uniform toilets in these passages.

sources.title: Lorenzo Castellano: Grapes and Wine in pre-Roman Anatolia (2023)
sources.note: Original author-uploaded full article read at ResearchGate publication 374802293; Journal of Near Eastern Studies 82(2), 171 to 196. Table 1 and pages 179 to 183: KH-P III 500 to 200 BCE, charred vine wood, seeds and pedicels; local vineyards strongly supported, specific wine-making by-product pathways hypothetical. DOI and author manuscript grouped.

sources.title: Lorenzo d’Alfonso: Celebrating Five Years of Excavating Kınık Höyük (NYU ISAW, 2015)
sources.note: Direct director’s report, Hellenistic textile tools, citadel/lower town, wall-niche vessel likely ritual wine use, accumulated dump. Broad Hellenistic observations are not assigned specifically to 300 BCE. Later refined fortification chronology from 2016 report takes precedence.

sources.title: Lorenzo d’Alfonso: Hellenistic-era Temple Found at Kınık Höyük (NYU ISAW, 2018)
sources.note: Direct excavation director’s report. Earlier sanctuary: late Achaemenid to middle Hellenistic bird vessels. Later monumental sanctuary and bulls separated; Dionysus identification explicitly tentative. Detailed 2023 chronology places monumental bovine figures in KH-P IIB after 200 BCE.

sources.title: Tacitus: Annals 2.42, translated by John Jackson, LacusCurtius
sources.note: Direct full primary passage. Archelaus summoned to Rome, dies, kingdom converted into province in 17 CE. Distinguish Tacitus’s hostile court narrative from securely stated administrative transition. No precise cause of death asserted.

sources.title: UNESCO: Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia
sources.note: Direct official statement. Rock-hewn Christian habitations and monasteries from fourth century CE; many decorated churches after 842. Used to prevent backdating Byzantine architecture to the Hellenistic map window.

proposedOverrides.name: Cappadocia: early kingdom and regional life
proposedOverrides.summary: Early Cappadocian rulers and regional communities, with a major imported-boundary caveat.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct indexed record -323 to -200, no alias. Keep Bithynia, Seleucid kingdom, Armenia and minor-states umbrella separate. Northern Pontic Cappadocia is not identical with the southern Ariarathid kingdom.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Identical world-bc 323 and world-bc 300 geometries; bbox 28.478,38.582,41.766,42.043. Gazioura, Amaseia, Ankara, Bursa inside. Mazaca, Tyana, Kınık Höyük, Göreme and sampled Sinope point outside. Public opening makes substantial geographic mismatch explicit; no corrected polygon asserted.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: ΑΡΙΑΡΑΜΝΟΥ, Ariaramnou, of Ariaramnes. Wroth 1899 xxv/PDF 23 Berlin bronze, visually checked; Shahbazi gives reading/gloss. Third-century rule, no exact issue year. Museum 1915,0407.15 is a separate comparative coin, not identified as that Berlin specimen.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Weiskopf Cappadocia article already near 200 cumulative words in minor-states; not used here. No fixed pan-regional founding year. Early Kınık layers differentiated from later defensive wall/bulls/Christian caves. No domestic kinship, universal literacy, toilets or healthcare reconstructed from absence.
